newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end lower on USDA crop estimates.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end lower on USDA crop estimates.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures closed lower on Monday after USDA's chief economist said U.S. soybean acreage could top 65 million acres in 1997, traders said.
That figure was above USDA estimates for 64 million acres released earlier Monday. Both figures were released during USDA's Outlook Conference in Washington.

USDA said soybean oil 1998 ending stocks were expected to climb to 2.445 billion lbs up from 1997 estimates for 1.965 billion. Soymeal 1998 ending stocks were forecast to reach 225 million short tons, compared with the 1997 estimates for 200 million tons.
The bearish figures outweighed news early Monday that warehouse workers at Brazil's Santos port were on strike over a dispute regarding back pay.
Union officials in Brazil said the strike would halt 90 percent of import activity and 70 percent of exports. But port sources said the stoppage would not affect exports at all.
Union members were expected to vote later Monday on a proposal by port authorities to resume work immediately.
Soymeal closed $1.30 to $0.10 per ton lower with March off $1.20 at $256.40. Soyoil ended down 0.40 to 0.25 per lb with March off 0.27 at 23.70.
Rosenthal Collins sold 500 lots May soymeal. Smith Barney bought 300 May and Chicago Corp bought 250 May and 200 March.
Prudential Securities reportedly spread 1,000 lots July/March soymeal while Cargill Inc spread 500 lots each March/July and May/August, traders said.
In soyoil, Griffin Trading and Rosenthal Collins each sold 500 lots May, FIMAT Futures sold 400 March and Iowa Grain sold 300 May, traders said.
Prudential Securities spread 800 lots March/July, Smith Barney spread 500 July/March and Dean Witter spread 300 March/July, traders said.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 26,000 lots, against Friday's actual volume of 30,090 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 17,000 lots, compared with Friday's volume of 22,522 lots.
